## Observed release failure (not a compromise claim) The resumed release published `pm-ops@2026.11.11` to npm, then refused its provenance because the expected signer identity came from the preparation run rather than the publishing job. - [Publishing run 43272393997 / job 131409063583](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ops/actions/runs/43272393997/job/131409063583), completed with failure, publishes merged commit `20aeecbd83f6d997576903c881940d459c9b5042`. - Job reports reusable workflow `daily-release.yml@refs/heads/main (20aeec...)`; trusted verifier checkout also resolves **20aeec**, not the preparation revision. - Candidate preparation run `43010127872/attempts/1` and tools pin are `831a0f01400ed352b75f01ed8ecf6e05b1308fe3`. - Job environment sets `PROVENANCE_SIGNER_WORKFLOW=unbraind/pm-ops/.github/workflows/daily-release.yml@831a0f01400ed352b75f01ed8ecf6e05b1308fe3`. - After registry visibility waits, Sigstore repeatedly reports certificate SAN mismatch: expected that SHA-qualified identity, observed `https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ops/.github/workflows/daily-release.yml@refs/heads/main`. Verification exhausts retries. ## Source and intended contract At [20aeec scripts/release-continuation.ts](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ops/blob/20aeecbd83f6d997576903c881940d459c9b5042/scripts/release-continuation.ts#L214-L221), continuation reads the **candidate preparation run**, validates its tooling SHA, and derives `signerWorkflow` from that run's referenced workflow path (only rewriting `@main`). The [workflow](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ops/blob/20aeecbd83f6d997576903c881940d459c9b5042/.github/workflows/daily-release.yml) forwards this as the publication verifier's signer expectation. [verify-registry-provenance.ts](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ops/blob/20aeecbd83f6d997576903c881940d459c9b5042/scripts/verify-registry-provenance.ts) accepts the supplied identity and [release-provenance.ts](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ops/blob/20aeecbd83f6d997576903c881940d459c9b5042/release-provenance.ts#L84-L90) enforces its exact SAN. Both verifier files were fetched at 831a0f and20aeec and are byte-identical; this is an identity-input mismatch, not evidence that the verifier should relax its check. Canonical [ops-release-continuation](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ops/blob/20aeecbd83f6d997576903c881940d459c9b5042/.agents/pm/issues/ops-release-continuation.toon) requires exact candidate/artifact/run/config bindings, cryptographic provenance, authenticated reusable signer, and independent certificate source repository/merged commit/ref checks. Preparation tool provenance and the signer of a later publication are distinct facts. ## Registry evidence and limits Read-only official npm metadata confirms version2026.11.11 and shasum `8be7e6fbd0bde5833202239e04d506b83ce79fd2`, matching the publish log; gitHead is absent. [Registry attestation](https://registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/attestations/pm-ops@2026.11.11) decoded SLSA claims match the registry SHA512 subject, commit20aeec, caller release.yml@refs/heads/main and publication run43272393997/attempts/1. These decoded claims were **not independently cryptographically authenticated** in this review and are not authorization to trust the artifact. No package execution, live publication, recovery mutation, or security-setting change was performed. Impact: an accepted npm upload remains blocked at release completion/verification, despite registry visibility. Repeating the same identity comparison cannot fix it. ## Acceptance / validation 1. Keep candidate preparation tooling SHA binding independent from the authenticated publishing workflow identity. 2. Resolve signer identity from authoritative evidence for the actual publication attempt, handling local reusable workflows and SHA-pinned external calls correctly. 3. Preserve fail-closed signature, transparency/trust-root, exact signer identity, certificate source repo/merged commit/ref, and subject digest checks. Do not trust decoded claims or broadly accept arbitrary refs. 4. Add regression coverage for preparation at831a0f followed by local reusable publication at20aeec/main; distinguish preparation pin, publishing workflow ref and implementation SHA. 5. Negative controls must still reject foreign signer/repository/commit/ref, altered digest/signature and missing/ambiguous run metadata. Include recovery of already-published versions without duplicate publication. 6. Validate against this read-only historical run/attestation and a cryptographically verified fixture; report fixture versus hosted evidence separately. Deduplication: all-status issues/PRs checked. #268 (sticky approval diagnosis) and #269 (candidate receipt parser) are distinct.
